title: Is Prediction Possible in General Relativity?
exact_version: Foundations of Physics 38 (2008) 317-321; DOI 10.1007/s10701-008-9204-6; received 16 Oct 2007, accepted 3 Jan 2008, published online 15 Jan 2008; Springer Science+Business Media LLC
relevance: Primary source for the draft's two Manchak appeals; exact hypotheses of the compact-slice theorem and the genuine-prediction verification-impossibility theorem
locator: Definition of P(q) p.318 with fn.6; Theorem 1 (compact, spacelike slice) p.319 with fn.9 (slice = closed achronal set without edge); fn.8 (Geroch's printed claim at [4,p.92] shown false by [6]=Hogarth 1993 pp.726-727); genuine-prediction definition and Theorem 2 (P(q) subset of boundary of J-(q)) pp.320-321; robustness remark under local field conditions p.321
assumptions: Standard spacetime (M,g); Geroch-style domain of prediction via achronal closed spacelike surface S in J-(q); for Theorem 2, embeddability of J-(q) into every inextendible spacetime
conclusion: Theorem 1: p in P(q) intersect I+(q) implies (M,g) admits a compact spacelike slice. Theorem 2: genuine prediction P(q) is contained in the boundary of J-(q); genuine prediction is essentially impossible
proof_status: authors' proofs read; not independently re-derived beyond checking proof sketches against hypotheses
dependencies: Wald 1984 (refs [8]: D(S) pp.200-201, Cauchy horizon p.203, initial-value chap.10), Hawking-Ellis 1973 (props 6.5.2-3, 6.6.6, 8.3.3), Geroch 1977, Hogarth 1993 (unread here)
limits: PhilSci preprint copy downloaded as backup but not text-compared page-by-page; Hogarth 1993 counterexample not read
open_questions: Whether the draft's Det(b) criterion implies Manchak's hypothesis for the closed dust model (not claimed by draft; not audited here)

conclusion: Domain of prediction framework; Einstein static universe allows direct verification of predictions; printed closed-universe claim (false as stated)

limits: OCR partially garbled on the equivalent-form sentence (wording reconstructed from context and cross-checked against Manchak's restatement); Fig.5 verified on printed p.91

title: FRW Universe Models in Conformally Flat Spacetime Coordinates. III: Universe models with positive spatial curvature
exact_version: arXiv:1103.4753v1 [gr-qc], 24 Mar 2011; journal version Eur. Phys. J. Plus 126 (2011) 30 (not accessed)
relevance: Primary confirmation that the closed-dust particle horizon vanishing at maximum expansion is prior work, as the draft states
locator: Sect.2.2 eqs.(11)-(15) (scale factor a = alpha(1-cos eta)+beta sin eta, cosmic time, max expansion eta2 = pi - arctan(beta/alpha)); p.4 'the whole universe can be seen at the moment of maximum extension. At this moment the particle horizon vanishes'; p.6 'horizon exists during the expansion era, and vanishes as the universe reaches its maximum size'; p.10 antipodal transformation identified as coordinate reflection only
assumptions: k=+1 FRW with dust+radiation; conformally flat coordinates
conclusion: Particle horizon disappears at maximum expansion (dust) / only at crunch (radiation); antipodal map appears as coordinate reflection without wave content
proof_status: authors' geometric derivation read; conformal-coordinate algebra not re-derived line-by-line
dependencies: refs [1,2] same series; Eriksen-Grøn de Sitter review
limits: v1 read, not the journal version; coordinate-domain subtleties (regions I/II) noted but not rechecked numerically

authors: Yu. L. Bolotin, I. V. Tanatarov

locator: Sect.1.4 problem 40(a) pp.21-22 (closed radiation a = a_m sin eta, particle horizon eta = chi, event horizon eta = pi - chi); problem 40(b) pp.22-23 (closed dust a = a_m(1-cos eta), particle horizon encloses full Universe at maximal expansion eta = pi and 'for later times does not exist'); Fig.1.10 caption p.22 (two light paths giving first and second images of a galaxy from opposite directions); bibliography ref [2] Rindler MNRAS 116 (6) 662-677 (1956)

limits: pages 1-23 + bibliography read; sections 1.5-1.9 (black holes etc.) outside scope

title: Caustics and wave propagation in curved spacetimes
authors: Abraham I. Harte, Theodore D. Drivas
exact_version: arXiv:1202.0540v3 [gr-qc], 6 Jun 2012; published Phys. Rev. D 85, 124039 (2012) (journal version not accessed)
relevance: Nearest published result to the echo proposition: universal sign-flip of retarded scalar Green functions at perfect caustics in conformally flat spacetimes (class including closed FLRW and ESU); canonical statement of Huygens failure on ESU-type backgrounds
locator: p.2 and p.28: 2-fold pattern delta(sigma) -> -delta(sigma) at anastigmatic caustics; 'Such patterns have indeed been observed in scalar Green functions for both the Einstein static universe and the Bertotti-Robinson spacetime [9]' with [9] = M. Casals, private communication (2012); p.28 'In the conformally-flat case, scalar Green functions have been computed in both the Einstein static universe and Bertotti-Robinson spacetimes [9]'; p.17 Sect.IV: Huygens principle special to plane waves, 'In almost all other cases, retarded Green functions have support inside the light cone [2,15]' with [2] Friedlander 1975, [15] Guenther 1988
assumptions: Linear scalar wave equations with d'Alembertian principal part in 4-d spacetimes; Penrose-limit correspondence
conclusion: Green-function singular structure flips sign at each multiplicity-2 caustic in conformally flat spacetimes; tails (Huygens violation) generic
proof_status: authors' full development read; Penrose-limit argument accepted, not re-derived
dependencies: Friedlander 1975; Guenther 1988; Ori 2009 unpublished; Casals et al. Nariai PRD 79 124043 (2009); Dolan-Ottewill PRD 84 104002 (2011)
limits: the ESU observation inside it rests on a private communication; not a published ESU Green-function computation
open_questions: Whether a printed ESU/closed-FLRW Green-function computation exists elsewhere (candidate: Casals-Dolan-Ottewill-Wardell papers)
